title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
statement: Digits 2-9 map to letters as on a phone keypad (2:abc 3:def 4:ghi 5:jkl 6:mno 7:pqrs 8:tuv 9:wxyz). Return every string you could type with a digit string, in any order. An empty input gives an empty list.

hints.1_question: Each digit offers a few letters; a result picks one letter per digit. How do you enumerate every such choice?
hints.2_nudge: Recurse over the digit positions; at each position try each letter of that digit and move on to the next digit.
hints.3_big_hint: bt(i, cur): if i == len(digits): record cur; else for c in letters[digits[i]]: bt(i + 1, cur + c). Return [] for empty input.

known_bugs.name: returns [''] for an empty input
known_bugs.followup: What should be returned when no digits are given?

known_bugs.name: gives 7 and 9 only three letters
known_bugs.followup: How many letters do the keys 7 and 9 have?

known_bugs.name: lists each digit's letters instead of combining them
known_bugs.followup: For '23' you should produce strings of length 2 such as 'ad'. What lengths does your output have?

followups: What is the output size for n digits in the worst case?
How would an iterative queue-based solution work?
